title: CISSP
subtitle: ISC2 CISSP · eight domains, April-2024 outline · think like a manager
releaseNote: beta.1 — 28 games. New adapters arrive each wave.
studyContext: I am studying for the ISC2 CISSP exam (April 2024 exam outline).
citeInstruction: Cite the CISSP exam outline domain and area (for example "Domain 7.6 — incident management") and, where relevant, the ISC2 CISSP Official Study Guide (10th edition) chapter, OWASP Top 10 2025 category, or MITRE ATT&CK tactic.

acceptedGaps.3.10: Information system lifecycle management is not drilled in beta.1. It is the one April-2024 area with no owner game: the campaign pool covers the other 61, and lifecycle governance did not fit any shipped board without becoming a policy quiz. Queued for the next content wave.

groups.label: Shift Command
groups.blurb: The flagship simulation — the whole outline, played under pressure instead of quizzed.

games.title: SOC Shift Command
games.blurb: Run the 23:00 to 07:00 shift: pick a specialty, rack two tools, and hold eight systems through a live adversary's night. Every miss becomes an incident you must contain.

games.title: Governance Foundations
games.blurb: Tell CIA, AAA, due care and due diligence apart before an exam question makes you.

games.title: Risk Math & Evidence
games.blurb: Name the metric or the evidence type — AV, EF, SLE, ARO, ALE, and what will stand up in court.

games.title: Boilerplate
games.blurb: Read one paragraph of governance prose and name what you are holding — policy, standard, guideline, procedure, or contract clause.

games.title: Risk Vocabulary, One Word Apart
games.blurb: Two near-identical governance scenes. One flipped detail decides who signs.

games.title: Risk Rush: Manager Mode
games.blurb: Eighteen fires on your desk. Pick the manager's FIRST move, not the technical fix.

games.title: Chain of Accountability
games.blurb: Owner, custodian, controller, processor, user, auditor — hand each duty to the role that actually holds the bag.

games.title: Borderlines
games.blurb: Pin GDPR, HIPAA, POPIA and their kin to the regimes that enforce them — then read what each one does to data crossing its border.

games.title: Classify or Die
games.blurb: Walk an asset from first label to final shred — mislabel it and the data walks out.

games.title: Intake Desk
games.blurb: New assets keep arriving. Route each one to the classification duty-holder who must act on it — owner, custodian, controller, or processor.

games.title: Whose Rule Is This?
games.blurb: Read the rule being enforced and name the model that wrote it.

games.title: Crypto Toolbox Triage
games.blurb: Five tools, five different problems. Send each requirement to the one built for it.

games.title: Crypto Locksmith
games.blurb: Choose the primitive the requirement actually needs, not the one you recognize.

games.title: Where Does This Control Belong?
games.blurb: Size a grant, stack a layer, re-verify a request — name the principle behind the control.

games.title: Crypto Graveyard
games.blurb: Bury each broken primitive in the decade that killed it — and read the attack on the headstone before the exam asks.

games.title: Network Foundations
games.blurb: Sort protocols, segments, wireless generations and the attacks that hunt them.

games.title: Layered Traffic
games.blurb: Rebuild the stack in order and put four classic attacks on the layer they hit.

games.title: Secure the Perimeter
games.blurb: A budget, a shop of real controls, one network. Place your defenses, then watch three attack waves resolve against what each control can actually do.

games.title: Models & Factors
games.blurb: Four access models, three factor types — decide which one each scene is exercising.

games.title: Federation, One Word Apart
games.blurb: SSO, federation, MFA — spot the single word that moves the answer.

games.title: Access Denied
games.blurb: Least privilege, separation of duties, provisioning gone wrong — one defensible answer each.

games.title: Audit Trail
games.blurb: Scan, test, audit, review, log check — say which one produced this finding, or which one is missing.

games.title: Resilience & Recovery
games.blurb: RTO, RPO, MTD, site tiers, backup schemes — the words that price a comeback.

games.title: Recovery, Minus One Detail
games.blurb: A metric, a site's readiness, a backup's chain — change one and the recovery plan changes.

games.title: Name That Attack
games.blurb: Ignore the tool. Name the ATT&CK tactic the intruder is serving right now.

games.title: Incident Zero
games.blurb: Order the response, the DR activation, the evidence chain — and the attacker's own path.

games.title: SDLC, Maturity & Testing
games.blurb: Place each scene on the methodology, maturity model or test technique it belongs to.

games.title: Patch Before Ship
games.blurb: Find what actually broke and file it under the right OWASP 2025 category before release.
